```{r tpl-setup, include=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# manuscript/_site_template.Rmd -- ONE page per site.
#
# This file is never rendered on its own. render_site.R writes a small wrapper
# per active site (site_<SLUG>.Rmd) that sets SITE_FOCUS and pulls this in as a
# child, so editing this file changes every site page at once.
#
# SITE_FOCUS is the only thing that varies. Everything below reads it and no
# other site, which is what keeps one site's numbers off another's page.
#
# Every section degrades: if the script that feeds it has not run for this site,
# it says so and names the script. It never errors.
# =============================================================================
source("_common.R")
stopifnot(exists("SITE_FOCUS"))
S <- SITE_FOCUS
```

```{r tpl-gate, results='asis'}
GATE_BOX(S)
```

## 1. The response, and the flow record

```{r tpl-response, results='asis'}
if (is.null(RESP)) NA_("the recruitment response has not been built", "R/01_build_response.R") else {
  m <- RESP$meta[RESP$meta$site == S, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(m)) NA_(paste0("site ", S, " is not in response.rds"), "R/01_build_response.R") else
    cat(sprintf(paste0("Recruitment is modelled as log(recruits / spawner) with a %d-year ",
                       "recruit lag against the `%s` node of the **null** (flow-naive) IPM ",
                       "posterior. Using the flow-informed fit here would make the ",
                       "flow-recruitment regression circular.\n\n"),
                RESP$rec_lag %||% NA, RESP$stock_node %||% "?"))
}
```

```{r tpl-f1, results='asis'}
FIG("01_f1a", S, "Response series with posterior uncertainty.")
FIG("02_f2a", S, "Daily discharge, standardized to log anomalies.")
```

Flow is standardized in three steps, in this order: logs, because discharge is
multiplicative; minus each day's mean across years, so a positive value means
wetter *than that date usually is*; then divided by **one** global standard
deviation. Dividing each day by its own SD would make a small wobble in a stable
week count the same as a doubling in June.

## 2. The weighted hydrograph, beta(t)

beta(t) is a weight for every day of the year. Score a hydrograph with it and the
sum is the predicted change in the response.

```{r tpl-beta, results='asis'}
FIG("03_f3a", S, "beta(t) for recruitment.")
FIG("03_f3b", S, "Probability that beta(t) is positive, by day.")
if (!is.null(BS)) FIG("04_f4a", S, "beta(t) for survival.")
```

```{r tpl-beta-note, results='asis'}
if (is.null(BR) || is.null(BR$fits[[S]])) NA_("beta(t) has not been fitted for this site",
                                              "R/03_fit_beta_recruitment.R")
```

## 3. Validation: is this a finding?

```{r tpl-gate-tbl}
g <- gate_rows(S)
if (is.null(g) || !nrow(g)) NA_("validation has not been run for this site", "R/05_validate.R") else
  TBL(g[, intersect(c("process","form","n_years","edf","r2_insample","r2_loo",
                      "r2_blocked","p_value","finest_p","passes"), names(g))],
      caption = "The gate. r2_blocked is the number that matters.")
```

Three numbers, failing in different ways. `r2_insample` is optimistic by
construction - the model has seen these years and spent `edf` degrees of freedom
on them. `r2_blocked` holds out contiguous blocks of years, so a test year's
neighbours are not in the training set; it can be negative, which means worse
than predicting the long-run mean. The gap between `r2_loo` and `r2_blocked` is
the autocorrelation leak that leave-one-out was flattering. `p_value` is a
permutation test whose smallest attainable value is `finest_p`; a p equal to
that floor means no permutation did as well, not that p is precisely that.

```{r tpl-f5, results='asis'}
FIG("05_f5a", S, "Cross-validated skill against the permutation null.")
```

## 4. When does water help?

```{r tpl-f6, results='asis'}
if (is.null(SE)) NA_("the daily sensitivity has not been run", "R/06_daily_sensitivity.R") else {
  FIG("06_f6a", S, "Benefit per cfs, by day.")
  FIG("06_f6b", S, "Where the benefit is concentrated.")
}
```

beta(t) is per standard deviation of log anomaly; a manager releases cfs.
Dividing by that day's baseline discharge **reshapes** the curve, because
discharge spans more than an order of magnitude across the year. The best day to
release water is often not the day with the largest beta(t).

### Can a single day honestly be named?

```{r tpl-intervals}
if (is.null(SE)) NA_("best-day intervals have not been computed", "R/06_daily_sensitivity.R") else {
  iv <- SE$intervals[SE$intervals$site == S, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(iv)) NA_("no interval rows for this site", "R/06_daily_sensitivity.R") else
    TBL(iv[, intersect(c("process","which","lo_month","median_month","hi_month",
                         "width_days","cred_level","resolvable"), names(iv))],
        caption = "If `resolvable` is FALSE, report a season. That is a property of the record.")
}
```

### The volume-constrained answer

```{r tpl-schedule}
if (is.null(DW)) NA_("the decision-window schedule has not been built", "R/06b_decision_window.R") else {
  sc <- DW$schedule[DW$schedule$site == S, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(sc)) NA_("no schedule rows for this site", "R/06b_decision_window.R") else
    TBL(sc[, intersect(c("process","volume_af","window_days","sustained_cfs",
                         "start_date","end_date","start_width_days","effect",
                         "p_positive","passes"), names(sc))],
        caption = "For a given volume and duration: when to start releasing, and what it buys.")
}
```

```{r tpl-f6b, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(DW)) { FIG("06b_f", S, "Benefit across the feasible release season.")
                    FIG("06b_h", S, "Every feasible schedule, scored.") }
```

## 5. What it does to the population

```{r tpl-production, results='asis'}
if (is.null(PR)) NA_("the production sensitivity has not been run", "R/07_production_sensitivity.R") else {
  FIG("07_f7a", S, "Change in surplus production by block of days.")
  p <- PR$production[PR$production$site == S & PR$production$pathway == "both", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(p)) print(TBL(p[order(-p$d_prod_pct), ][1:min(6, nrow(p)),
                          intersect(c("month","block_start","block_end","d_prod_pct",
                                      "d_biomass","p_positive"), names(p))],
                         caption = "The six most productive blocks, whole-population."))
}
```

## 6. Bureau of Reclamation scenarios

```{r tpl-scen, results='asis'}
SC <- if (S %in% (CFG$sites$bor %||% character(0))) SCEN(S) else NULL
if (!(S %in% (CFG$sites$bor %||% character(0)))) {
  cat("\n> **DATA NOT AVAILABLE** - there is no BoR forecast hydrograph for this\n",
      "> site. That is different from finding no effect: the question was not\n",
      "> asked here.\n\n", sep = "")
} else if (is.null(SC)) {
  NA_("this site has a BoR forecast but no scenario results", "R/08_scenarios_bor.R")
}
```

```{r tpl-scen-tbl}
if (!is.null(SC))
  TBL(SC$effects[, intersect(c("Scenario","Period","Type","process","n_years","effect",
                               "across_years_lo","across_years_hi","p_negative",
                               "frac_extrap","status"), names(SC$effects))],
      caption = "Effect of each scenario relative to the historical mean hydrograph.")
```

```{r tpl-scen-fig, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(SC)) {
  FIG("08_f8a", S, "Scenario effects.")
  FIG("08_f8b", S, "Which DAYS make a scenario better or worse.")
  cat("\nThe day-by-day attribution is the more useful panel. A scenario can hurt",
      "because flow drops on days the fish care about, or because it drops a lot on",
      "days they do not - and those call for different responses. The single",
      "number cannot tell them apart.\n\n")
  if ("frac_extrap" %in% names(SC$effects) && max(SC$effects$frac_extrap, na.rm = TRUE) > 0.1)
    cat("\n> **Extrapolation.** Some scenario-years sit outside anything in the\n",
        "> training record on more than 10% of days. beta(t) is unconstrained there.\n",
        "> Read those rows as projections, not predictions.\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## 6b. Equilibrium under a sustained scenario

```{r tpl-rule, results='asis'}
RC <- if (S %in% (CFG$sites$bor %||% character(0))) RULE(S) else NULL
if (is.null(RC)) NA_("the rule-curve arm has not been run for this site", "R/10_rulecurve.R")
```

```{r tpl-rule-tbl}
if (!is.null(RC))
  TBL(RC$summary[, intersect(c("Scenario","Period","Type","n_years","mean_Q","mean_z",
                               "K","dK_pct","MS","dMS_pct","frac_extrapolating",
                               "frac_K_finite"), names(RC$summary))],
      caption = "Equilibrium abundance K and maximum surplus production, held at each scenario's flow.")
```

```{r tpl-rule-fig, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(RC)) {
  FIG("10_a", S, "The replacement line.")
  cat("\nSection 6 asks what a year like this does. This section asks what this flow",
      "regime does if held indefinitely, which is a different question and can point",
      "the other way: a scenario that is mildly bad every year compounds at",
      "equilibrium.\n\n")
  if ("frac_K_finite" %in% names(RC$summary) && any(RC$summary$frac_K_finite < 0.9))
    cat("\n> **K undefined in more than 10% of draws for at least one scenario.** The\n",
        "> replacement curve does not cross the 1:1 line there, so the LEVEL of K is\n",
        "> not trustworthy. The change may still be.\n\n", sep = "")
}
```
